controls.title: Policies for information security
controls.description: The organization should define its information security policy along with topic-specific policies, obtain management approval for them, publish them, communicate them to relevant staff and stakeholders for acknowledgement, and re-examine them at regular intervals or whenever major changes take place.

controls.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Roles and responsibilities pertaining to information security should be established and assigned in line with what the organization requires.

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.description: Duties and areas of responsibility that conflict with one another should be kept separate.

controls.title: Management responsibilities
controls.description: Management is expected to direct all personnel to apply information security in line with the organization's established information security policy, topic-specific policies, and procedures.

controls.title: Contact with authorities
controls.description: Contacts with the appropriate authorities should be set up and kept active by the organization.

controls.title: Contact with special interest groups
controls.description: Organizations are encouraged to create and sustain relationships with special interest groups.

controls.title: Threat intelligence
controls.description: Data concerning information security threats should be gathered and evaluated in order to generate threat intelligence.

controls.title: Information security in project management
controls.description: Project management should incorporate information security considerations.

controls.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
controls.description: A record of information and related assets, together with their designated owners, should be created and kept up to date.

controls.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
controls.description: Guidelines governing the proper use and handling of information and its related assets should be determined, written down, and put into practice.

controls.title: Return of assets
controls.description: When employment, a contract, or an agreement ends or changes, staff and other stakeholders must hand back every organizational asset they hold.

controls.title: Classification of information
controls.description: Information should be assigned classifications that reflect the organization's security requirements with respect to confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

controls.title: Labelling of information
controls.description: Suitable procedures for labelling information should be created and applied consistent with the scheme used to classify information.

controls.title: Information transfer
controls.description: Rules, procedures, and controls governing information transfer should be in place to safeguard information shared both internally and with outside parties.

controls.title: Access control
controls.description: Based on business and security needs, rules governing both physical and logical access to information and assets should be set up and enforced.

controls.title: Identity management
controls.description: The complete life cycle of digital identities — covering their registration, upkeep, and eventual removal — should be managed within the organization.

controls.title: Authentication information
controls.description: A formal management process should govern how authentication information is issued and administered, and should include guidance for staff on handling it correctly.

controls.title: Access rights
controls.description: Access rights to information and assets should be granted, periodically reviewed, adjusted, and revoked in line with the organization's policy on access control.

controls.title: Information security in supplier relationships
controls.description: Processes and procedures should be defined and put in place for handling information security risks that arise from using suppliers' products or services.

controls.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
controls.description: Relevant information security requirements should be established and mutually agreed with every supplier, according to the nature of the relationship with that supplier.

controls.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
controls.description: Processes and procedures should be established and applied to address information security risks connected to the supply chain for ICT products and services.

controls.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
controls.description: Suppliers' information security practices and service delivery should be monitored, reviewed, and evaluated on a recurring basis, with any changes managed accordingly.

controls.title: Information security for use of cloud services
controls.description: Processes covering the acquisition, use, management, and exit of cloud services should be established in line with the organization's information security requirements.

controls.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
controls.description: Preparation for managing information security incidents should include defining, setting up, and communicating the relevant incident management processes, roles, and responsibilities.

controls.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
controls.description: Information security events should be evaluated to determine whether they qualify as information security incidents.

controls.title: Response to information security incidents
controls.description: Responses to information security incidents should follow the procedures that have been documented.

controls.title: Learning from information security incidents
controls.description: Lessons learned from information security incidents should be applied to reinforce and enhance information security controls.

controls.title: Collection of evidence
controls.description: Procedures should be established and applied for identifying, gathering, acquiring, and preserving evidence connected to information security events.

controls.title: Information security during disruption
controls.description: Plans should be made for keeping information security at a suitable level throughout periods of disruption.

controls.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
controls.description: ICT readiness should be planned, put into effect, kept current, and tested in line with business continuity goals and the requirements for ICT continuity.

controls.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements
controls.description: Requirements arising from law, regulation, and contracts that relate to information security, together with the organization's approach to satisfying them, should be identified, recorded, and kept up to date.

controls.title: Intellectual property rights
controls.description: Suitable procedures should be put in place by the organization to safeguard intellectual property rights.

controls.title: Protection of records
controls.description: Records must be safeguarded against loss, destruction, falsification, and access or disclosure by unauthorized parties.

controls.title: Privacy and protection of PII
controls.description: Requirements for preserving privacy and protecting PII should be identified and fulfilled in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and contractual obligations.

controls.title: Independent review of information security
controls.description: An independent review of the organization's information security management approach and its implementation — covering people, processes, and technology — should take place at planned intervals or following major changes.

controls.title: Compliance with policies, rules, and standards for information security
controls.description: Adherence to the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, rules, and standards should be reviewed on a regular basis.

controls.title: Documented operating procedures
controls.description: Operating procedures for information processing facilities should be written down and made accessible to the personnel who require them.

controls.title: Screening
controls.description: Before joining the organization — and on a continuing basis thereafter — all prospective personnel should undergo background verification checks. These checks should comply with applicable laws, regulations, and ethical standards, and be proportionate to business needs, the classification of the information to be accessed, and the perceived risks.

controls.title: Terms and conditions of employment
controls.description: Contracts of employment should specify the information security responsibilities of both the employee and the organization.

controls.title: Information security awareness, education and training
controls.description: Staff and other relevant stakeholders should be given suitable information security awareness, education, and training, along with regular updates on the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, and procedures, appropriate to their job roles.

controls.title: Disciplinary process
controls.description: A formal disciplinary process should be established and communicated so that action can be taken against staff or other relevant stakeholders who violate information security policies.

controls.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
controls.description: Information security duties and responsibilities that continue to apply after employment ends or changes should be specified, enforced, and communicated to the affected personnel and other stakeholders.

controls.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
controls.description: Organizations are required to identify, document, and periodically review confidentiality agreements or non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) that adequately address their information protection needs.

controls.title: Remote working
controls.description: This control advises organizations to adopt a policy that guarantees secure access to information systems and networks for those working away from the office.

controls.title: Information security event reporting
controls.description: Organizations must establish a mechanism through which staff can promptly report information security events they observe or suspect, using the proper channels.

controls.title: Physical security perimeter
controls.description: Safeguards should be in place to stop unauthorized physical access, damage, or interference affecting the organization's information and other associated assets.

controls.title: Physical entry controls
controls.description: Suitable entry controls and access points should be used to safeguard secure areas.

controls.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
controls.description: Physical protection measures for offices, rooms, and facilities should be designed and put in place.

controls.title: Physical security monitoring
controls.description: Continuous monitoring of premises should be maintained to detect unauthorized physical access.

controls.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
controls.description: Measures guarding against physical and environmental threats — including natural disasters and other deliberate or accidental physical threats to infrastructure — should be designed and implemented.

controls.title: Working in secure areas
controls.description: Appropriate security measures for those working within secure areas should be designed and put into practice.

controls.title: Clear desk and clear screen
controls.description: Rules requiring desks to be cleared of papers and removable storage media, and screens to be cleared on information processing equipment, should be established and properly enforced.

controls.title: Equipment siting and protection
controls.description: Equipment should be positioned in secure locations and given appropriate protection.

controls.title: Security of assets off-premises
controls.description: Assets located away from the organization's premises should be safeguarded.

controls.title: Storage media
controls.description: Storage media should be managed throughout their entire life cycle — from acquisition through use, transportation, and disposal — in line with the organization's classification scheme and handling requirements.

controls.title: Supporting utilities
controls.description: Safeguards should protect information processing facilities against power outages and other disruptions resulting from failures in supporting utilities.

controls.title: Cabling security
controls.description: Cables carrying power, data, or supporting information services should be shielded against interception, interference, and damage.

controls.title: Equipment maintenance
controls.description: Proper maintenance of equipment is required to preserve the availability, integrity, and confidentiality of information.

controls.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
controls.description: Before equipment containing storage media is disposed of or reused, checks should confirm that any sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or securely overwritten.

controls.title: User endpoint devices
controls.description: Information that is held on, processed by, or reachable through user endpoint devices must be safeguarded.

controls.title: Privileged access rights
controls.description: Privileged access rights should be limited and carefully managed in both their allocation and use.

controls.title: Information access restriction
controls.description: Access to information and other associated assets should be limited in line with the established topic-specific policy on access control.

controls.title: Access to source code
controls.description: Both read and write permissions for source code, development tools, and software libraries should be properly controlled.

controls.title: Secure authentication
controls.description: Authentication technologies and procedures that are secure should be deployed in accordance with information access restrictions and the topic-specific policy on access control.

controls.title: Capacity management
controls.description: Resource utilization should be tracked and tuned to match both present and anticipated capacity needs.

controls.title: Protection against malware
controls.description: Anti-malware protections should be deployed and reinforced by suitable user awareness efforts.

controls.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.description: The organization should gather information on technical vulnerabilities affecting its information systems, assess its exposure to those weaknesses, and take suitable measures in response.

controls.title: Configuration management
controls.description: The configurations of hardware, software, services, and networks — including their security settings — should be defined, documented, applied, monitored, and reviewed.

controls.title: Information deletion
controls.description: When information held in information systems, devices, or any other storage media is no longer needed, it should be deleted.

controls.title: Data masking
controls.description: The application of data masking should follow the organization's topic-specific policy on access control, other related topic-specific policies, and business needs, while also respecting applicable legislation.

controls.title: Data leakage prevention
controls.description: Measures to prevent data leakage should be deployed across systems, networks, and any other devices that handle, hold, or transmit sensitive information.

controls.title: Information backup
controls.description: Backup copies of information, software, and systems should be kept and tested at regular intervals, consistent with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.

controls.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
controls.description: Redundancy adequate to satisfy availability requirements should be built into information processing facilities.

controls.title: Logging
controls.description: Logs capturing activities, exceptions, faults, and other relevant events should be generated, retained, safeguarded, and analysed.

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.description: Anomalous behaviour in networks, systems, and applications should be monitored, with suitable actions taken to assess potential information security incidents.

controls.title: Clock synchronisation
controls.description: Clocks on the information processing systems used by the organization should be kept in sync with approved time sources.

controls.title: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.description: Utility programs capable of bypassing system and application controls should have their use restricted and closely supervised.

controls.title: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.description: Procedures and safeguards should be put in place to manage software installation on operational systems securely.

controls.title: Network security
controls.description: To protect the information held in systems and applications, networks and network devices should be secured, managed, and controlled.

controls.title: Security of network services
controls.description: The security mechanisms, service levels, and service requirements of network services should be determined, put in place, and kept under observation.

controls.title: Segregation of networks
controls.description: Within the organization's networks, information services, users, and information systems should be separated into distinct groups.

controls.title: Web filtering
controls.description: Access to websites outside the organization should be controlled to limit exposure to harmful content.

controls.title: Use of cryptography
controls.description: Rules governing the effective application of cryptography — including the management of cryptographic keys — should be established and enforced.

controls.title: Secure development life cycle
controls.description: Rules covering the secure development of software and systems should be defined and put into practice.

controls.title: Application security requirements
controls.description: When applications are being developed or acquired, their information security requirements should be identified, detailed, and formally approved.

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.description: Principles for the secure engineering of systems should be defined, documented, kept up to date, and applied across all information system development activities.

controls.title: Secure coding
controls.description: Software development should follow principles of secure coding.

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.description: Processes for security testing should be established and embedded within the development life cycle.

controls.title: Outsourced development
controls.description: Activities connected to system development that has been outsourced should be guided, monitored, and reviewed by the organization.

controls.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
controls.description: Environments used for development, testing, and production should be kept apart from one another and appropriately protected.

controls.title: Change management
controls.description: Any changes to information processing facilities and information systems should go through formal change management procedures.

controls.title: Test information
controls.description: Information used for testing should be carefully chosen, protected, and managed.

controls.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
controls.description: Audit tests and similar assurance activities that assess operational systems should be planned and mutually agreed between the tester and the relevant management.
